brief.data: Imported sleep records: 274 nights from 14 Feb to 15 Nov 2026, each with total sleep (median 6 h 52 m), deep sleep minutes (median 61, range 18–104), wake-ups, resting heart rate and a 1–5 self-rated restfulness score. 41 nights are missing deep-sleep data. The coffee log has 612 entries with time, cup size and type (drip, espresso, decaf). The draft experiment is called 'Noon cutoff', with condition A (last caffeine by 12:00) and condition B (last caffeine by 16:00), alternating 7-day phases for 4 weeks, and a primary outcome of deep sleep minutes. There are 2 active warnings: washout under 10 days and outcome night-to-night variation of ±22 minutes. The app's help library covers 18 concepts, including washout, blinding, baseline period, confounders and minimum detectable effect. Setup progress is at 3 of 6 steps.

prompt:
I need the front end for Tally & Trial. An inexpensive personal app for curious people who want to run careful single-person experiments on their own habits, such as caffeine, bedtime or exercise timing, and see whether a change actually made a difference.

Who's using it: Desmond Achebe, 63, a retired land surveyor who likes numbers and keeps a sleep diary for fun. He bought Tally & Trial last night after reading an article on self-experimentation. He is new to the app and to experimental design terms, though he is very comfortable with spreadsheets.

What they're doing right now: He has just finished importing nine months of sleep data exported from his fitness watch, plus his own coffee log, and is setting up his first experiment: does stopping caffeine at noon instead of 4 pm improve his deep sleep? He has drafted two alternating one-week phases. The app flagged that his phases are shorter than the recommended washout period and that his outcome measure is 'noisy', and he doesn't understand either warning. He wants to understand what's being asked of him, fix the design, and get the experiment started tonight without reading a manual.

What's in the system at this point: Imported sleep records: 274 nights from 14 Feb to 15 Nov 2026, each with total sleep (median 6 h 52 m), deep sleep minutes (median 61, range 18–104), wake-ups, resting heart rate and a 1–5 self-rated restfulness score. 41 nights are missing deep-sleep data. The coffee log has 612 entries with time, cup size and type (drip, espresso, decaf). The draft experiment is called 'Noon cutoff', with condition A (last caffeine by 12:00) and condition B (last caffeine by 16:00), alternating 7-day phases for 4 weeks, and a primary outcome of deep sleep minutes. There are 2 active warnings: washout under 10 days and outcome night-to-night variation of ±22 minutes. The app's help library covers 18 concepts, including washout, blinding, baseline period, confounders and minimum detectable effect. Setup progress is at 3 of 6 steps.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
